title: Martin Shkreli livestreamed himself violating lifetime pharma ban, FTC says
gist: The FTC and seven states asked a federal judge to hold Martin Shkreli in contempt for allegedly trading pharma stocks and discussing the industry on livestreams despite his lifetime pharma ban, seeking divestiture, disgorgement and escalating penalties.

insights.claim: The FTC and attorneys general of New York, California, Illinois, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Virginia asked a federal judge to hold Shkreli in contempt for allegedly violating the 2022 lifetime pharma ban 'flagrantly and repeatedly' nearly since it began.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A regulator pursuing a livestreaming trader under an industry ban is a test of how enforcement reaches social-media market commentary.
insights.locator: On Tuesday, the FTC and the seven states

insights.claim: The ban explicitly bars Shkreli from owning pharma stock and making public statements that could influence a pharma company's business; remedies sought include forced divestiture, a fine equal to trading profits, and escalating penalties including incarceration.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Disgorgement of trading profits sets a precedent for penalizing influencer-driven trading violations.
insights.locator: With the alleged violations, the FTC and the states are now seeking

insights.claim: FTC Commissioner Mark Meador says a lifetime industry ban is only effective if breaches are met with proportionate consequences.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Signals the Trump-era FTC is willing to pursue enforcement against high-profile violators.
insights.quote: A lifetime industry ban is only effective if breaches are met with consequences commensurate with the seriousness of the order.

insights.claim: Shkreli responded that he could see NY AG Letitia James limiting free speech but not 'Trump's FTC', framing the case as a free-speech issue.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The free-speech defense will likely be the legal battleground over restricting commentary under the ban.

themes.theme: Alleged trading pattern and market impact

insights.claim: The filing details four phases of alleged violations: a 2022 trading competition, shorting a small biotech in 2024, a 2025 challenge shorting three small biotechs, and a $10 million account challenge begun in June 2026.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Repeated gamified trading challenges show a persistent retail-audience model built around biotech shorts.
insights.locator: The brief filed by the FTC and the states

insights.claim: In 2025 Shkreli told viewers to short a pharma company and its stock reportedly dropped 17 percent quickly, and he described a 'magic trick' that he can always find a couple of biotech stocks to 'smoke'.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Small-cap biotech prices can move on a single influencer's call, a market-manipulation risk to monitor.
insights.quote: It doesn't matter what trades I make because I can always find a couple of biotech stocks to smoke.

insights.claim: The agencies say the livestreamed stocks are 'likely the tip of the iceberg', since FTC staff reviewed only a fraction of his activity and he has referenced other accounts.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Undisclosed accounts imply the true scale of trading may be larger than currently alleged.
